p10.why: A recognisable table moment with a sharp turn ('they read his clock') that any player has felt from both sides of the table.

p17.why: Names a moment the viewer has lived and probably blamed on the cards, then moves the villain to the strategy they think is safe.

p24.why: A small, familiar scene with the numbers inside it: you won 1.5 and paid 9.75, a stake felt in one breath.

p06.why: Everyone who has played tight knows this deflating moment, told as a scene in eleven words.

p29.why: Turns the viewer's own virtue ('discipline') into a question they have to answer about last session.

p13.why: Flips the tight player's frustration into something he can use, in one short line that sounds wrong at first.

p37.why: A familiar urge after a long wait, told from inside the viewer's head, with the mistake about to happen.

p18.why: A short contradiction of what tight players believe about their best hands.

p26.why: Calls out the belief that folding is free and answers it with a number every player pays.

p16.why: A then-vs-now arc most players recognise in themselves, funny in eight words.
